summary: Mission Forge is a web-based aerospace mission-concept design and analysis platform. It brings spacecraft budgeting, trajectory exploration, NASA data, team collaboration, and mission reporting into one workspace. Users can compare spacecraft mass, power, cost, and propulsion trade-offs; explore transfer opportunities using JPL Horizons data and Lambert-based trajectory analysis; and inspect available Deep Space Network activity and NASA TechPort projects. The platform also supports collaborative design, deterministic FDIR findings from available telemetry, and a Gemini-powered CAPCOM assistant that provides advisory—not operational—recommendations. Mission dossiers can be generated as PDF and JSON for review and sharing.
details: Mission Forge is an aerospace mission-concept design and analysis web application for teams exploring preliminary interplanetary missions. It brings mission configuration, engineering trade-offs, trajectory analysis, collaboration, and reporting into one workspace. Users can create mission designs, review spacecraft components and their data provenance, and assess supported mass, power, cost, propulsion, and communications budgets. The Astrodynamics Lab uses JPL Horizons data and Lambert/porkchop analysis to explore transfer opportunities across departure and arrival windows. Users can inspect NASA Deep Space Network ground-link activity and NASA TechPort technology-project information where those services are available. Mission Forge also provides a multi-role Concurrent Design Facility for sharing design changes, a deterministic FDIR interface for presenting supported anomaly findings and telemetry-quality states, and a Gemini-powered CAPCOM assistant that provides bounded, advisory recommendations. The CAPCOM assistant does not control a spacecraft or create, suppress, or replace deterministic FDIR findings. The application can generate mission dossier PDF and JSON outputs from the selected mission design. The project combines a React and TypeScript frontend with a Python/FastAPI backend and engineering visualization tools. NASA and JPL data are identified by source and are distinguished from static metadata, cached information, calculations, and simulated or unavailable data. Trajectory outputs are preliminary analyses with documented assumptions; they are not flight-qualified plans or NASA-certified results. Super Intelligence was used to assist software development and to provide the optional Gemini-based CAPCOM advisory. Team members reviewed and tested the implementation. AI recommendations are presented as advisory information and do not replace engineering judgment or deterministic safety logic.
